Batch 6, STANDARD-queue position 5 of seed 6102026. C17's THIRD locked item. C17-006's only item, and the batch's FIRST standard-stratum item since C03-04 (positions 2, 3 and 4 were all excluded).

ONE ITEM, NOT TWO -- AND MY OWN FIRST READING SAID TWO, WHICH IS CORRECTED HERE RATHER THAN QUIETLY DROPPED. I proposed splitting this under section 4.3.2 (self-performance against a duty to bind a third party) on the strength of its SURFACE SHAPE, 'shall provide, or shall cause ... to provide', without reading section 4.3.2's own worked case. THE CONNECTIVE IS THE WHOLE RULING, and it was checked by execution: C04-139's span, read from C04-04's JSON, is 'Bellicum shall use, AND will cause its Subcontractors and Licensees to use, Miltenyi Products ...' -- CONJUNCTIVE, both performances required, each independently breachable, which is why it splits into two items. THIS clause reads 'Company shall provide, OR shall cause ... to provide' -- DISJUNCTIVE, two ALTERNATIVE MODES of discharging ONE duty. Performing either discharges it, so neither limb is independently breachable and section 4.3's splitting test returns ONE item. Asserted at write time: the regex for 'shall provide,\s*or\s*shall cause' must match, so a future edit cannot silently turn this back into a conjunctive reading.

SO THIS IS SECTION 10.1 F28's CLASS -- a disjunctive obligation, one duty with alternative performances and the obligor choosing between them -- and F28's own row already states it is NOT section 4.3's shape for exactly this reason: 'failing to negotiate is not a breach if you modified instead, so splitting would assert two duties where the contract imposes one'. F28 is NOT MINTED, so no tag is available and `known_gaps` is EMPTY.

WHICH LIMB IS ANNOTATED, and it is decided by F28's SECOND rule rather than its first. There is NO PRIMACY SIGNAL: no performance adverb attaches to either limb, verified rather than eyeballed -- contrast C04-10, which turned on 'promptly and diligently' attaching to one limb. So C04-10's textual-primacy test has no input here, exactly as at C04-12. C04-12's STRUCTURAL rule governs: ANNOTATE THE LIMB WHOSE PERFORMANCE IS THE OBLIGOR'S OWN. Limb 1 is Company providing, so obligor and performance align; limb 2's substantive performance belongs to the Affiliates or third parties, Company's own act being only 'causing', and annotating it would seat a causer in the obligor slot against another party's act. Limb 1, PROVIDE.
AND THIS IS THE SECOND CONSECUTIVE F28 INSTANCE WITH NO PRIMACY SIGNAL, which is worth recording because it bears on F28's own open question: 2 of its 3 instances give C04-10's primacy test no input at all. That does not falsify the test -- C04-10's own signal was real -- but it is evidence that the structural rule is doing most of the work in practice.

F28's STILL-WANTED CASE IS *NOT* DISCHARGED BY THIS ITEM, and the check is recorded so a future session does not have to redo it. F28 asks for 'one where the TEXTUALLY PRIMARY limb is the OFF-TAXONOMY one', that being the only configuration testing whether C04-10's primacy test is real or merely convenient. Here BOTH limbs are on-taxonomy -- limb 1 `provide` -> PROVIDE, limb 2's own act `cause` -> ENSURE/PROCURE, all three verified members of ACTIONS -- so the configuration does not arise and the row stays open.

THE COST IS DISCLOSED RATHER THAN LEFT TO BE FOUND, and it runs TWO ways because this item carries BOTH untagged structural gaps:
  (1) F28: with `known_gaps` empty the item ENTERS section 9.1's in-force criterion-2 denominator while carrying a disjunction `Obligation.action` cannot represent -- the IR asserts a duty to PROVIDE where the contract permits discharge by causing another to provide, which is F28's own OVERSTATING direction.
  (2) F25: this is the THIRD locked item sitting in that denominator with an untagged, unrepresentable `DURING`-family temporal, after C10-03 and C04-15. 'During the applicable Term of any Service' returns None through the production `_classify_temporal()` (gated on a known accept first), and it is unrepresentable on SLOT ARITY -- `DuringTemporal` demands two bound references and the text supplies one named period, the same analysis recorded in full at C04-14's notes. NOT filed as F25 instance two or three in F25's own CLASS sense: that row is scoped to EVENT-BOUNDED intervals and this is a defined-term period, section 8's own separate `during the Term` row. `temporal: null`, untagged.
BOTH COSTS ARE LATENT: C17-006 has no cassette, so the item is cassette-unscoreable and no published figure moves today.

'IN ACCORDANCE WITH THE TERMS AND CONDITIONS OF THIS AGREEMENT' IS SECTION 10.1 F36's CLASS -- ITS SECOND INSTANCE, AND IT DISCHARGES F36's FORCING FUNCTION. The phrase asserts CONFORMITY, which is subordination's grammatical work rather than a carve-out's, so it falls on F36's side of the boundary that row drew at C03-125 ('the boundary is the phrase's grammatical work, not its vacuity'). Section 3.8's removal test returns nothing: delete it and the duty is still governed by the agreement's terms, because it IS a term of the agreement. NOT a `conditions` entry. F36 asked for 'a second instance where the vacuous phrase sits in a span whose item is otherwise in the in-force denominator' -- and this item's `known_gaps` is EMPTY, so it IS in that denominator. THE FORCING FUNCTION IS MET. Reviewer-ruled that NO AMENDMENT follows now: the answer (not a conditions entry) is unchanged, and what F36 holds open is only whether section 3.8's binary should gain an explicit third outcome.

'SUBJECT TO SECTION 2.2' IS MANNER, NOT A CONDITION. It qualifies WHICH third parties may be used to provide the services -- a constraint on the permitted mode of performance rather than a circumstance in which the duty applies. Section 3.8's removal test: delete it and Company still owes the services in the identical circumstances; only the set of permissible providers broadens. Distinct from F36's phrase in that it is a SPECIFIC cross-reference rather than vacuous self-reference, and section 2's cross-reference row does not exclude on it because no SCORED field's value depends on resolving Section 2.2 -- `action`, `object_class`, both parties and `temporal` are all determinable with it unresolved.

UNDERSPECIFIED true / missing_fields ['obligor'] -- AND THIS FIELD WAS WRONG IN MY FIRST DRAFT, CAUGHT BY THE HARNESS'S OWN R5 SELF-CHECK WITHIN MINUTES OF THE RISK BEING FLAGGED. I drafted `underspecified: false` while simultaneously writing into these notes that the registry's aliases carry the article ('the Company', 'The Company') where this span's token is bare 'Company', and that whether it resolves was 'a real question for the first scoring run'. The first scoring run answered it immediately: `run_scoring.run()` REFUSED TO SCORE with 'R5 self-check failed ... [C17-03] UNDERSPECIFIED MISMATCH: annotated False, but section 3.9 over registry C17 computes True. Parties: obligor=\'Company\' does not resolve.' So bare `Company` does NOT resolve -- `resolve_party()` matches aliases EXACTLY, and section 21 R2's trap is about CASE rather than about articles, so neither alias covers the bare token.
THE ITEM IS CORRECTED, NOT THE REGISTRY, and that choice is deliberate. Section 3.9 trigger 1 is mechanical: a party NAMED in the span but not registry-resolvable makes the item underspecified, which is exactly how C04-16's `the Parties` is annotated (underspecified true, obligor in missing_fields) against the same C04 registry holding only Miltenyi and Bellicum. Section 3.5 also requires the alias VERBATIM from the span, so `Company` is the right value and cannot be silently rewritten to `the Company` to make it resolve.
WHETHER THE REGISTRY SHOULD GAIN A BARE `Company` ALIAS IS A REAL QUESTION AND IS DELIBERATELY NOT ANSWERED HERE. Editing a committed registry mid-annotation-pass is the wrong moment -- the same posture CLAUDE.md records for the registries' stale `status` field -- and it would change how OTHER C17 items resolve, so it needs its own verification rather than riding along in an item's drafting. Recorded so the next session that touches evals/registry/C17.json sees it.
`obligee` RGHI DOES resolve (an exact alias of Reynolds Group Holdings Inc.), and `temporal` is null, so F15's predicate -- NOT(obligor resolves AND obligee resolves AND temporal is null) -- gives underspecified TRUE on the obligor limb alone.
